subject: Draft Charter Amendments Review
overview: The Medford Charter Study Committee reviewed the remaining articles of the draft charter, debating language with representatives from the Collins Center. The committee approved several amendments concerning School Committee vacancies, publication requirements, budget timelines, and dual office-holding approvals.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes of the August 1, 2024 meeting.

items.title: Article 4: Term of Office Language
items.summary: Voted to standardize the School Committee term-of-office language in Section 4.1 to match provisions for the City Council and Mayor.

items.title: Article 4: District Eligibility Residency Requirements
items.summary: Voted to require candidates to reside in their district for one year prior to inauguration and to allow School Committee members who move within Medford during their term to finish out their service.

items.title: Article 4: Filling School Committee Vacancies
items.summary: After an initial tie vote, the committee approved language specifying that unfilled School Committee vacancies be filled jointly by the City Council and School Committee.

items.title: Articles 5 and 9: Public Notice and Publication Requirements
items.summary: Approved a motion requiring that charter-mandated public notices be published both in a newspaper and on the city website, defeating an amendment to use broader media language.

items.title: Article 6: Annual Budget Meeting Date
items.summary: Voted to move the required annual joint budget meeting date from on or before March 1st to on or before February 15th.

items.title: Article 6: Capital Improvement Procedures
items.summary: Reviewed Collins Center capital improvement provisions in Section 6-5 and agreed to retain the language as drafted.

items.title: Article 7: Elections and Statements of Candidates
items.summary: Discussed the definition of candidate statements under Section 7.2 and retained the standard state election law language without amendment.

items.title: Article 8: Citizen Participation, Recall, and Initiatives
items.summary: Withdrew proposed amendments regarding recall grounds and confirmed Section 8.2 already requires the solicitor's opinion to be mailed to petitioners.

items.title: Article 9: Residency Requirement for Multi-Member Bodies
items.summary: Agreed to ensure previously approved language establishing a residency requirement and council waiver process for appointed boards is incorporated into the draft.

items.title: Article 9: Dual Office Holding and City Council Approval
items.summary: Approved an amendment requiring mayoral waivers for individuals holding more than one city office or position to be submitted to the City Council for approval, taking effect if the council does not act within 30 days.

items.title: Article 9: Section 9.11 City Clerk Oath Correction
items.summary: Agreed to remove reference to an elected city clerk taking an oath of office under Section 9.11 because the position is not elected.

items.title: Article 9: Financial Disclosure and Ethics Commission
items.summary: Defeated an amendment to strike Section 9.18, thereby retaining charter language establishing financial disclosure requirements and an ethics commission.

items.title: Article 4: School Committee Bill Review Duties
items.summary: Voted to restore deleted language assigning the School Committee secretary the duty of overseeing and approving school department bills unless a dedicated subcommittee is formed.

items.title: Final Report Subcommittee Update
items.summary: Reviewed the schedule for finalizing the draft charter and report with the Collins Center ahead of the committee's final meeting in October.
